The new framework is focused initially on Kuwait, Qatar, Saudi Arabia, and the United Arab Emirates and is organized around three areas: technology, digital resilience, and people. Microsoft said it will pursue the initiatives with partners in the region from now until 2030. Microsoft said it has served the Middle East since it began operations in the region in 1991, growing from a local technology provider into a long-term partner to governments, businesses, educational institutions, and civil society organizations. Under the technology pillar, Microsoft said it will continue to invest in cloud and AI infrastructure across the region, expanding capacity, launching new capabilities, and delivering long-term infrastructure commitments. The company said it will deepen strategic partnerships with governments and national AI champion organizations, building on existing work with HUMAIN , G42, QAI, and the Government of Kuwait. The company cited digital-government initiatives including TAMM in the UAE, SDAIA’s ALLaM in Saudi Arabia, TASMU in Qatar, and Microsoft 365 Copilot adoption across the Government of Kuwait. Microsoft said the partnerships will support responsible AI adoption, sovereign-ready cloud services, Arabic and multilingual AI, and the use of AI to improve services for citizens and businesses, supported where relevant and available by capabilities including Microsoft Sovereign Public Cloud, Sovereign Private Cloud, and Project Digital Shield. Microsoft said it plans to invest more than $400 million in subsea and terrestrial connectivity across the Middle East by 2030, an investment it said will expand capacity, strengthen regional data flows, and support its growing cloud and AI infrastructure footprint in the region. The company said it has invested in major international subsea cable systems, including SeaMeWe-6, which has landings in Qatar, Saudi Arabia, and the UAE, and operates a global network spanning more than 275,000 miles of terrestrial and subsea fiber. Describing redundancy as “the foundation of continuity,” Microsoft said that during network disruptions it has rerouted traffic through Middle East corridors and maintained service continuity with minimal impact on customers. On sustainability, Microsoft said that as it expands cloud and AI infrastructure in the four countries it will work with lessor partners to advance its water-positive ambitions, including prioritizing zero-water cooling technologies where feasible, guided by the company’s global goals on carbon, water, waste, and ecosystems. Microsoft said it will also work with governments and local stakeholders to identify opportunities for responsible water stewardship across the region and will collaborate with regulators, utilities, and lessor partners to help create the market conditions needed to expand carbon-free electricity procurement and stimulate new clean energy investment. Microsoft said it will launch a new Middle East digital resilience initiative built around digital resilience assessments, reference architectures, readiness guidance, continuity planning, and enablement programs intended to help organizations identify vulnerabilities, protect critical data, and build tested recovery capabilities. The company said conflict in the Middle East has reinforced the connection between digital resilience and digital sovereignty, and that it will make digital resilience a cornerstone of its Middle East strategy. The company will expand its existing commitments on data-protection sovereignty and business continuity to eligible governments and customers in Kuwait, Qatar, Saudi Arabia, and the UAE, complemented by its sovereign-cloud portfolio. Microsoft also said it is deepening partnerships with the cybersecurity authorities in the four countries, and that a network of dedicated Microsoft cybersecurity champions in the four countries will help governments connect national priorities with expertise across Microsoft. Microsoft said it will expand collaboration with the Responsible AI Future Foundation, which it co-founded with G42 and the Mohamed bin Zayed University of Artificial Intelligence, to support the development and sharing of responsible AI practices and evaluation tools for high-impact AI use cases. The company’s AI for Good Lab will continue regional research and partnerships focused on food security, low-resource language development, and climate and disaster resilience, including the LINGUA program, which supports the development of language technologies for underserved communities. Under the people pillar, Microsoft said it will continue to invest in AI skills, workforce readiness, public-sector capability building, and inclusive talent development across Kuwait, Qatar, Saudi Arabia, and the UAE, building on existing commitments to help skill more than 4.2 million people by 2030. The work includes training for public-sector leaders, students, and workers; initiatives focused on expanding opportunities for women; and partnerships with educational institutions across the region. Existing programs cited by the company include Saudi Arabia’s AI Global Leadership Program, AI Skills 4 Women programs in Saudi Arabia and Qatar, and the Women’s Datacenter Academy in Saudi Arabia. Microsoft said it is working with governments, educators, institutions, and partners to develop responsible AI principles across primary, secondary, and tertiary education, including supporting AI literacy, helping educators integrate AI into teaching and learning, and sharing practical guidance for responsible AI use in educational settings. Microsoft said it will also partner with governments, employers, workers, education providers, and other stakeholders on practical skills development, workforce readiness, and leadership development, and will engage with workforce coalitions that support national talent strategies and policy recommendations. Microsoft said it has been part of the region’s journey for more than 35 years and is committed to being a partner for the long term. Protecting subsea and terrestrial connectivity requires sustained cooperation between governments and the private sector, but the foundation of continuity is redundancy. A diverse network of high-capacity routes allows traffic to be rerouted around disruptions, minimizing latency and maintaining critical data flows.

Microsoft has helped expand both the capacity and reliability of digital connectivity across regions through investments in major international subsea cable systems, including SeaMeWe-6, which has landings in Qatar, Saudi Arabia, and the United Arab Emirates, as well as operating a global network spanning more than 275,000 miles of terrestrial and subsea fiber. During network disruptions, Microsoft has demonstrated the value of redundancy by rerouting traffic through Middle East corridors and maintaining service continuity with minimal impact on customers.

Building on this foundation, Microsoft plans to invest more than $400 million in subsea and terrestrial connectivity across the Middle East by 2030. This investment will expand capacity, strengthen regional data flows, and support Microsoft’s growing cloud and AI infrastructure footprint across the region.
We will build AI infrastructure with the planet in mind

As we expand our cloud and AI infrastructure in Kuwait, Qatar, Saudi Arabia, and the UAE, we will do so with a focus on responsible growth. Guided by Microsoft’s global goals to address carbon, water, waste, and ecosystems, we will work with our lessor partners to ensure that the cloud infrastructure supporting our services advances Microsoft’s water-positive ambitions, including by prioritizing zero-water cooling technologies where feasible.

Water resilience is particularly important across the Middle East. Building on Microsoft’s global experience advancing water stewardship through water reuse, replenishment, and innovative water management solutions, we will work with governments and local stakeholders to identify opportunities that advance responsible water stewardship across the region.

As AI accelerates economic opportunity across the Middle East, expanding access to clean energy will be essential to ensuring this growth is sustainable. We will also collaborate with regulators, utilities, and our lessor partners to help create the market conditions needed to expand carbon-free electricity procurement and stimulate new clean energy investment. By combining infrastructure investment with local partnerships and innovation, we aim to support the region’s energy and water priorities while helping build the sustainable foundations needed for long-term AI-led economic growth.
We will launch a new Middle East digital resilience initiative

Conflict in the Middle East has reinforced the connection between digital resilience and digital sovereignty. Microsoft has worked with customers to support business continuity through resilience options tailored to different operational and regulatory needs. Going forward, Microsoft will make digital resilience a cornerstone of its Middle East strategy, helping organizations strengthen continuity and recovery through digital resilience assessments, reference architectures, readiness guidance, continuity planning, and enablement programs that help identify vulnerabilities, protect critical data, and build tested recovery capabilities.
We will strengthen data protection, privacy, and business continuity

Microsoft will expand our existing commitments on data-protection sovereignty and business continuity to eligible governments and customers in Kuwait, Qatar, Saudi Arabia, and the UAE. These are designed to give organizations greater confidence in how their data, systems, and operations are protected while maintaining continuity in times of uncertainty. They will be complemented by Microsoft’s growing sovereign-cloud portfolio, including Sovereign Public Cloud and Sovereign Private Cloud capabilities, together with Project Digital Shield and other capabilities that support security, privacy, transparency, and operational resilience.
We will expand and strengthen cybersecurity cooperation

As Kuwait, Qatar, Saudi Arabia, and the UAE accelerate their digital transformation, cybersecurity has become a core pillar of national and economic security. As governments, critical infrastructure, and economies become more connected, cyber threats and influence operations can have consequences that extend far beyond physical borders. That’s why we are announcing that we are deepening our partnerships with the cybersecurity authorities in these countries.

A network of dedicated Microsoft cybersecurity champions in Kuwait, Qatar, Saudi Arabia, and the UAE will help governments translate these resources into action and connect national priorities with expertise across Microsoft. Stronger cybersecurity benefits far more than individual networks. It helps build trust to ensure digital transformation will succeed.
We will advance responsible AI through governance, assurance, and inclusion

Microsoft will work with governments, businesses, researchers, and civil society organizations across the Middle East to help people and institutions benefit from new technology. As AI advances, realizing its full potential will require not only access to powerful technology, but the governance, assurance, and skills required to deploy it confidently and responsibly.

We will help strengthen AI governance capabilities across the region and support practical approaches to testing, evaluating, and assurance systems. We will also expand collaboration with the Responsible AI Future Foundation (RAIFF), co-founded with G42 and the Mohamed bin Zayed University of Artificial Intelligence (MBZUAI), to support the development and sharing of responsible AI practices and evaluation tools that can be applied across high-impact AI use cases in the Middle East and beyond.
We will advance AI for Good research and innovation

Microsoft’s AI for Good Lab will continue to support the region through research and partnerships focused on food security, low-resource language development, and climate and disaster resilience. This includes work through initiatives such as the LINGUA program, which supports the development of language technologies for underserved communities.

In partnership with governments, NGOs, nonprofits, and research institutions, the AI for Good Lab will continue developing and scaling AI solutions that address real-world challenges across the Middle East and beyond.
We will prepare the next generation for the AI economy

We believe AI should enhance human ambition, strengthen human capability, and help prepare workers to thrive in a changing economy. That is why Microsoft will continue to invest in AI skills, workforce readiness, public-sector capability building, and inclusive talent development across Kuwait, Qatar, Saudi Arabia, and the UAE, building on existing commitments to help skill more than 4.2 million people by 2030.

This work includes training for public-sector leaders, students, and workers; initiatives focused on expanding opportunities for women; and partnerships with educational institutions across the region. This work builds on programs such as Saudi Arabia’s AI Global Leadership Program, AI Skills 4 Women programs in Saudi Arabia and Qatar, and the Women’s Datacenter Academy in Saudi Arabia. Microsoft will also engage with workforce coalitions that can support national talent strategies and policy recommendations.
We will help education communities prepare learners for the AI era

Microsoft is working with governments, educators, institutions, and partners across the Middle East to develop responsible AI principles across primary, secondary, and tertiary education. This includes supporting AI literacy, helping educators integrate AI into teaching and learning, and sharing practical guidance for responsible AI use in educational settings. Across Kuwait, Qatar, Saudi Arabia, and the UAE, we will work with local partners to ensure students and educators can benefit from AI safely, responsibly, and effectively and will engage educators, policymakers, industry leaders, and civil society to support practical approaches to AI implementation that reflect local priorities.
We will help empower workers in the AI economy
We will support local and national AI talent priorities across the Middle East

Microsoft is partnering with governments, academic institutions, and civil society organizations to support national talent priorities by advancing AI skills, leadership development, and workforce readiness programs for public-sector leaders, students, underrepresented talent, and people across the Middle East. The goal is to help countries build globally competitive workforces, accelerate innovation, and unlock new economic opportunities in the AI era.

extraction.body: Feds know of 5 crashes where cars using comma.ai devices hit slow or stopped vehicles. Aftermarket devices that can boost or augment a vehicle’s native advanced driver assistance systems are the target of a new federal investigation this week. The National Highway Traffic Safety Administration’s Office of Defects Investigation says it knows of five crashes in which drivers using devices from comma.ai crashed into stopped or slow-moving cars. Two of the crashes resulted in three deaths, and 11 people were injured in four of the five crashes, some seriously. Comma.ai was the brainchild of George Hotz, who rose to prominence at the start of the last decade by jailbreaking iOS and hacking Sony PlayStations. In 2015, Hotz turned his attention to partially automated driver assists, which were gaining attention following Tesla’s exploits with its Autopilot system. Hotz first modified his own Acura to give it a more advanced driver assist that let him take his hands off the wheel, with the goal of selling his system to Tesla and replacing Mobileye as the company’s supplier. (Mobileye dropped Tesla as a customer the following year after becoming unhappy with the way the car company was using Mobileye products in unintended ways.) Comma’s first attempts to sell devices that owners could plug into their cars’ ODB port evaporated once NHTSA began asking questions in 2016 . Instead, Comma decided to post its openpilot software, as well as its plans for hardware, to GitHub, allowing anyone to make the devices themselves . At first, the Comma Neo and OpenPilot supported a single Acura and single Honda model, but by 2020, the company’s software and $999 device were rated more highly by Consumer Reports than any OEM system. Now, Comma says the Comma Four can add lane centering, adaptive cruise, and a cloud-based dash cam to more than 325 models of car across 27 different brands. More than 30,000 drivers are using openpilot, with more than 402 million miles (650 million km) driven. But NHTSA isn’t sure that Comma’s systems are able to adequately detect a slow or stopped car in the path of travel. At least two of the five crashes involved a comma.ai-controlled car hitting a stopped vehicle; in one case, it was a first responder’s vehicle, and the resulting crash killed three. Another of the five crashes saw a comma.ai-controlled car hit a vehicle that was merging, hence this preliminary evaluation. NHTSA says it is also interested in which version of the software was running at the time of each crash—at least two involved forks of the main build, including the fatal crash, which was running a version called FrogPilot . extraction.body: A device that promises hands-off driving for cars people already own is under federal scrutiny. The National Highway Traffic Safety Administration opened a preliminary investigation on September 21 into devices made by Comma AI, the startup founded by security hacker George Hotz, who is no longer managing day-to-day operations but remains a major owner. Regulators said vehicles equipped with the devices struck slow-moving or stopped vehicles in their lanes. Eleven people were injured, and three people died across the five reported crashes, according to the Office of Defects Investigation. "ODI has confirmed that the systems were powered on or engaged in multiple crashes," NHTSA wrote. "Preliminary data reviewed by ODI suggests that the comma system may not have adequately detected or responded to the in-lane vehicles." Authorities also plan to determine what kind of software was running during each crash, adding that some vehicles may have used modified versions, known as forks, of Comma AI's open-source software. The software in question involves comma three, comma 3X, comma four, and OpenPilot. Comma AI sells an aftermarket device that brings its driver-assistance system to more than 325 car models. The company's website states that the system can steer, accelerate, and brake, and said that it "can drive for hours without intervention." The website also tells drivers to stay alert and ready to take control at any time, and includes a driver-monitoring system that alerts when it detects driver distraction. One crash described in the NHTSA reporting appears to match a February incident in Louisiana. A state police report said a Toyota RAV4 hit an unoccupied police vehicle that was stopped in a highway lane with its emergency lights on, and two passengers in the Toyota died. The police did not identify the driving software in their account of the crash. Other autonomous driving systems and companies have faced investigations over the past few years. NHTSA in 2021 investigated Tesla's Autopilot and said that Teslas using the system struck vehicles stopped at first-responder scenes. There is also an open investigation into Waymo for striking a child near a school in Santa Monica. In July, NHTSA also issued a broader warning to driverless-vehicle developers about vehicles entering emergency scenes or blocking ambulances and firefighters. Comma AI's own support information lists stationary vehicles in the same lane among conditions that can affect OpenPilot's adaptive cruise control. Comma AI did not immediately respond to a request for comment.

In 2023, Tesla recalled over 2 million vehicles in the US to better ensure drivers pay attention when using its Autopilot driver assistance system after NHTSA opened a probe after identifying more than a dozen crashes in which Tesla vehicles hit stationary emergency vehicles.
NHTSA said vehicles with Comma devices reportedly struck five stopped or slow-moving vehicles.
Comma.ai says the devices that use open source software can allow for hands-free driving and reports more than 30,000 vehicles have logged 402 million miles with the devices.
In 2016, NHTSA demanded that Comma.ai provide proof to regulators that its proposed device for self-driving cars would be safe, or risk having its sale blocked.

extraction.body: Feds know of 5 crashes where cars using comma.ai devices hit slow or stopped vehicles. Aftermarket devices that can boost or augment a vehicle’s native advanced driver assistance systems are the target of a new federal investigation this week. The National Highway Traffic Safety Administration’s Office of Defects Investigation says it knows of five crashes in which drivers using devices from comma.ai crashed into stopped or slow-moving cars. Two of the crashes resulted in three deaths, and 11 people were injured in four of the five crashes, some seriously. Comma.ai was the brainchild of George Hotz, who rose to prominence at the start of the last decade by jailbreaking iOS and hacking Sony PlayStations. In 2015, Hotz turned his attention to partially automated driver assists, which were gaining attention following Tesla’s exploits with its Autopilot system. Hotz first modified his own Acura to give it a more advanced driver assist that let him take his hands off the wheel, with the goal of selling his system to Tesla and replacing Mobileye as the company’s supplier. (Mobileye dropped Tesla as a customer the following year after becoming unhappy with the way the car company was using Mobileye products in unintended ways.) Comma’s first attempts to sell devices that owners could plug into their cars’ ODB port evaporated once NHTSA began asking questions in 2016 . Instead, Comma decided to post its openpilot software, as well as its plans for hardware, to GitHub, allowing anyone to make the devices themselves . At first, the Comma Neo and OpenPilot supported a single Acura and single Honda model, but by 2020, the company’s software and $999 device were rated more highly by Consumer Reports than any OEM system. Now, Comma says the Comma Four can add lane centering, adaptive cruise, and a cloud-based dash cam to more than 325 models of car across 27 different brands. More than 30,000 drivers are using openpilot, with more than 402 million miles (650 million km) driven. But NHTSA isn’t sure that Comma’s systems are able to adequately detect a slow or stopped car in the path of travel. At least two of the five crashes involved a comma.ai-controlled car hitting a stopped vehicle; in one case, it was a first responder’s vehicle, and the resulting crash killed three. Another of the five crashes saw a comma.ai-controlled car hit a vehicle that was merging, hence this preliminary evaluation. NHTSA says it is also interested in which version of the software was running at the time of each crash—at least two involved forks of the main build, including the fatal crash, which was running a version called FrogPilot . passages: Meta Platforms CEO Mark Zuckerberg rejected calls for an industry-wide slowdown in frontier AI development, arguing that trust and alignment will become competitive requirements for successful models.
Meta's approach also links safety to how frontier labs allocate infrastructure.
Zuckerberg said labs should direct a "significant majority" of compute toward serving users rather than pursuing recursive self-improvement, although he did not disclose a target percentage.
Meta's August essay, "The Future is for Everyone," placed this strategy within a broader argument for distributing advanced AI rather than concentrating it among a handful of labs or governments.
Zuckerberg said competing agents aligned with different users would create checks on centralized power.
Yahoo Finance is not a broker-dealer or investment adviser and does not offer securities or cryptocurrencies for sale or facilitate trading.

Zuckerberg's position leaves safety decisions primarily with individual labs, supported by market incentives, liability and outside evaluation.
It also preserves Meta's ability to continue expanding models and infrastructure without waiting for competitors to adopt a common development schedule.
Muse operates in an isolated environment inside Meta's computing infrastructure and asks permission before sensitive actions.
Meta has also subjected the agent to internal testing and agentic red-teaming, while soliciting outside security research through a bug-bounty program.

Meta reported $31.1 billion of capital expenditures in the second quarter and guided to $130 billion to $145 billion for 2026, with investment going toward server capacity, data-center facilities and networking infrastructure.
The company has said capacity will remain tight as demand grows across model training, consumer agents and enterprise products.
Zuckerberg said Meta Superintelligence Labs already uses independent evaluators and advisers in several areas.

sources.title: Everything new coming to Meta’s AI agent Muse
passages: Meta says it is bringing Muse computer work to Mac.
The company had previously talked about Muse coming to Mac , and spent more time on Wednesday providing a few new details.
This means that users will be able to delegate tasks to the agent, and — much like other popular AI agents from OpenAI and Anthropic — Muse will be able to operate any app on a user’s desktop.
The agent is powered by Muse Spark , Meta’s multimodal AI model built for agentic work.
Meta has touted it as a more accessible agent than those offered by competitors — an AI helper that, from the jump, allows users to automate the busy work in their lives.
Since Muse will always be working in the background, it will naturally need its own email address.
Meta’s Wang announced it is developing that feature and will make it available “soon,” without providing a more precise timeline.
Meta’s personal AI agent Muse is only a few weeks old, and the social networking giant isn’t wasting any time building out what may be its biggest bet on consumer AI to date.

“The centerpiece of our vision for what we’re building is Muse,” Zuckerberg said as he kicked off a keynote donning khakis and a black T-shirt with the words “Building is My love Language” emblazoned across the front. “In the coming years, I expect that Muse is going to grow into the personal superintelligence that billions of people around the world are going to use to accomplish their goals and improve their lives.”
There’s certainly a hint of Metaverse-ishness to this feature, which was demoed on stage at Connect.
Muse will also be integrated with Meta’s smart glasses line , the company announced.
Wang noted that the company wants Muse to connect with small business too.

Meta recently opened its platform to allow developers to build their own “connectors.” The company received more than 1,500 applications in less than week, he said, adding “I think this could be a generational opportunity to start building for a new platform as it takes off, and the response so far has been really great.”

Muse can access the entire Shopify product catalog agentically and use Lync and now Shop Pay to buy almost anything on the internet, according to Wang, who noted that Meta has also added more support for payments with PayPal.
The Muse agent (the physical avatar is named Jolly, according to Zuckerberg) is designed to handle everyday tasks by connecting to users’ apps and services, including email and calendars.
At Connect, Zuckerberg introduced a slew of new capabilities and integrations to make Muse more useful and more deeply woven into users’ daily lives.
Zuckerberg also believes that Muse will make money for its users — and of course, eventually for Meta.

At Connect, Zuckerberg introduced a slew of new capabilities and integrations to make Muse more useful and more deeply woven into users’ daily lives. This means that users will be able to delegate tasks to the agent, and — much like other popular AI agents from OpenAI and Anthropic — Muse will be able to operate any app on a user’s desktop.

sources.title: Meta’s Muse AI agent fuels chip stock rally as AMD hits $1 trillion market cap - Crypto Briefing
passages: Meta ’s personal AI agent, Muse, has done something unusual for a software launch: it moved the entire semiconductor sector.

AMD crossed the $1 trillion market cap threshold for the first time, Intel surged roughly 12%, and Arm Holdings popped about 17%, all on the back of what is essentially a very smart digital assistant that can book your flights and fill out forms.
Meta is also exploring commerce opportunities tied to Muse.
AMD’s 10% jump to a $1 trillion valuation is particularly notable.
The company has been chasing that milestone while competing against Nvidia in the data center GPU market.
Ironically, it was a CPU-heavy workload that finally pushed it over the line.
Meta launched Muse on September 8, 2026, in the US for adults 18 and older.
It rolled out across iOS, Android, the web at muse.ai, and WhatsApp.
Within 13 days, it sat atop the App Store free charts.
Meta has explicitly kept in-app ads out of Muse, at least for now.
Instead, the company is monetizing through subscriptions: a free tier, a $20 per month plan, and a $100 per month premium option.
Muse’s launch didn’t happen on schedule.
Meta originally targeted April 2026 but delayed the rollout to improve safety and reliability.
Intel’s 12% rally deserves its own footnote.
A world where CPU-intensive AI workloads grow faster than expected is arguably the most favorable macro environment Intel could ask for.
Agentic AI, the category Muse belongs to, involves sequential, multi-step tasks: checking your email, cross-referencing your calendar, booking a restaurant, then sending a confirmation.
These workloads are more CPU-intensive than the parallel processing that GPUs excel at.
That distinction matters enormously for companies like AMD and Intel, which have spent years watching Nvidia capture the lion’s share of AI infrastructure spending.

At Connect, Zuckerberg introduced a slew of new capabilities and integrations to make Muse more useful and more deeply woven into users’ daily lives. Muse will be everywhere, if the user chooses, including on their Meta AI glasses. Muse, which launched in early September, interacts across a user’s devices and digital accounts. Here are the new features and capabilities that got our attention … One of the more fun announcements made Wednesday is that Muse users will soon have the ability to conjure a distinct digital avatar for their particular agent and then video chat with it in real time. A new AI model, Muse Realtime Avatar, has been developed to power the particular feature, the company says. The idea is that Meta’s previously faceless AI software will be given a face, body, and voice, making them significantly more personable. There’s certainly a hint of Metaverse-ishness to this feature, which was demoed on stage at Connect. Users will be able to have live conversations with this avatar, giving it tasks and asking it questions. Muse will also be integrated with Meta’s smart glasses line , the company announced. This means that users will be able to communicate with their agent merely by speaking to their glasses. The agent activates via a wake word, the company said, adding that it will be able to guide users through a personalized workout, log meals, book an appointment, and help them buy products they see. Meta said Muse will work in the background and check back in when it’s done. sources.title: Meta’s Muse AI agent fuels chip stock rally as AMD hits $1 trillion market cap - Crypto Briefing
passages: Meta ’s personal AI agent, Muse, has done something unusual for a software launch: it moved the entire semiconductor sector.

AMD crossed the $1 trillion market cap threshold for the first time, Intel surged roughly 12%, and Arm Holdings popped about 17%, all on the back of what is essentially a very smart digital assistant that can book your flights and fill out forms.
Meta is also exploring commerce opportunities tied to Muse.
AMD’s 10% jump to a $1 trillion valuation is particularly notable.
The company has been chasing that milestone while competing against Nvidia in the data center GPU market.
Ironically, it was a CPU-heavy workload that finally pushed it over the line.
Meta launched Muse on September 8, 2026, in the US for adults 18 and older.
It rolled out across iOS, Android, the web at muse.ai, and WhatsApp.
Within 13 days, it sat atop the App Store free charts.
Meta has explicitly kept in-app ads out of Muse, at least for now.
Instead, the company is monetizing through subscriptions: a free tier, a $20 per month plan, and a $100 per month premium option.
Muse’s launch didn’t happen on schedule.
Meta originally targeted April 2026 but delayed the rollout to improve safety and reliability.
Intel’s 12% rally deserves its own footnote.
A world where CPU-intensive AI workloads grow faster than expected is arguably the most favorable macro environment Intel could ask for.
Agentic AI, the category Muse belongs to, involves sequential, multi-step tasks: checking your email, cross-referencing your calendar, booking a restaurant, then sending a confirmation.
These workloads are more CPU-intensive than the parallel processing that GPUs excel at.
That distinction matters enormously for companies like AMD and Intel, which have spent years watching Nvidia capture the lion’s share of AI infrastructure spending.

Meta launched Muse on September 8, 2026, in the US for adults 18 and older. It rolled out across iOS, Android, the web at muse.ai, and WhatsApp. Within 13 days, it sat atop the App Store free charts.

Muse runs on Meta’s proprietary Muse Spark models and operates inside isolated secure virtual machines with user-controlled permissions. The architecture is designed to let the agent perform sensitive tasks, like making purchases or filling out forms with personal data, without exposing that information to Meta’s broader advertising infrastructure.

Meta has explicitly kept in-app ads out of Muse, at least for now. Instead, the company is monetizing through subscriptions: a free tier, a $20 per month plan, and a $100 per month premium option.
Muse’s launch didn’t happen on schedule. Meta originally targeted April 2026 but delayed the rollout to improve safety and reliability.

The company has projected capital expenditures between $130-$145 billion for 2026, a staggering figure even by Big Tech standards. It also recently absorbed an $18 billion settlement. Meta is also exploring commerce opportunities tied to Muse. An AI agent that can autonomously complete purchases creates a natural transaction layer that could eventually complement Meta’s existing advertising business.

Intel’s 12% rally deserves its own footnote. The company has struggled to keep pace with AMD and Nvidia in recent years, cycling through turnaround plans and leadership changes. extraction.body: XRP Leads Crypto Losses as Ethereum, Dogecoin Prices Crater Alongside Bitcoin XRP was the worst-performing altcoin among the leading cryptocurrencies Thursday morning, showing a 15% drop over the last 24 hours as markets swing bearish and Bitcoin extends its losses . At the time of writing, XRP was trading for $1.30 after having dropped roughly 28% in the past week, according to crypto price aggregator CoinGecko. An earlier dip to $1.28 marked the lowest price for the Ripple-linked asset since November 2024, when XRP surged in the wake of President Trump's election win. It's also the biggest daily drop of any coin in the top 100 cryptocurrencies by market cap over the last day. Ethereum was recently trading at $1,985 after plunging 6% on the day and losing about 30% of its value in the last week, while original meme coin Dogecoin is down about 8% on the day to $0.09, shedding nearly 19% of its value over the past seven days. BNB was recently changing hands for $666 after having dropped 9% in the past day, losing 23% in the past seven days. Solana had dipped to $85, after falling about 8% in the past day, and was 27% lower than it was this time last week. Bitcoin dove below the $67,000 mark Thursday morning, but was recently trading just above $68,000. The drawdown has resulted in the liquidiation of more than $47 million worth of XRP derivatives contracts. And the bulk of them, nearly $44 million worth, were long on XRP, according to on-chain analytics platform CoinGlass. Overall, more than $1.43 billion worth of crypto positions have been liquidated in the last day. The platform also shows that XRP trading volume has jumped by 57%, with over $11 billion worth of coins changing hands in the past 24 hours. The global crypto market capitalization has now fallen 7.4% on the day to $2.37 trillion after having peaked above $4.2 trillion in September 2025. Meanwhile, XRP treasury firm Evernorth now has a $446 million unrealized loss on its 388,710,631 XRP stash. The company debuted as an XRP treasury in October, saying that its goal was to raise more than $1 billion to buy XRP. It also has backing from Ripple, whose executives are acting as strategic advisors to the firm. In late October, the company spent $947 million buying XRP. It hasn't made another buy since then, but it has watched the value of its XRP holdings drop sharply to approximately $501 million. The company didn't immediately respond to a request for comment from Decrypt . XRP ETF inflows slowed down, but didn't turn red yesterday. The seven spot XRP ETFs that are trading in the U.S. saw $5.9 million in volume and net inflows of $6.9 million on Wednesday, according to an ETF tracker maintained by XRP Insights. Ripple Labs CEO Brad Garlinghouse has been outspoken about the "absolute firestorm of action to get the Market Structure bill passed," but hasn't commented on markets going bearish. Crypto traders are broadly feeling skittish about current market conditions. The Crypto Fear & Greed Index maintained by CoinGlass has dropped to 11, firmly in the "Extreme Fear" category. During the month of January, it very briefly ticked into the greed category when the index peaked at 62, but has been steadily declining since then. passages: Finding the best crypto to buy now is on the radar of many investors as crypto markets are at an inflection point in September 2026.

Bitcoin has consolidated below its all-time high, yet institutional inflows via ETFs remain structurally positive, and Ethereum’s Pectra and Glamsterdam upgrades are actively reshaping its throughput.
The markets are beginning to pick up with capital inflowing into the sector.
For investors entering now, the key question isn’t whether to buy crypto; it’s which assets match your time horizon and risk appetite.
September 2026 has seen an impressive crypto rally with Bitcoin leading the charge.
Bitcoin has shot from $60,000 to $85,000 in just two weeks.

Bitcoin has plenty of momentum, is leading the crypto charge, and we are seeing Bitcoin ETF inflows in the positive, leading investors to expect Bitcoin still has some room to run and possibly reclaim the coveted $100,000 price point.
XRP has one of the strongest and most loyal fan bases in all of crypto, and with the September 2026, the “XRP Army” is in full force, propelling the asset over 10% in just 7 days.
As memecoins continue to outperform many other crypto projects, Dogecoin is the most recognized “blue chip” memecoin that ends up taking most of the liquidity.
If you want to invest in established crypto projects (a.k.a. dino coins ), look at their past price charts and how they handled tough periods, such as the 2022–2023 crypto winter.
Cardano has chosen a different route than the path followed by Ethereum and Solana.
Cardano is a research-focused blockchain led by a highly technical team that prioritizes compliance and technological accuracy over speed and marketing.
This is evident in Cardano’s 100% uptime and interest expressed by governments and academic institutions.
There’s no one “best” crypto for a $1,000 investment.
Conservative investors consider Bitcoin or Ethereum as core long‑term holdings, while growth-oriented investors prefer smaller‑cap tokens for their upside potential despite the higher risk.
Ethereum is mid-cycle in a meaningful upgrade sequence.
Pectra (live since May 2026) already increased validator staking limits and improved wallet UX.
The Glamsterdam fork , targeting mid-2026, is designed to push transaction capacity well beyond its current ceiling.
What this means practically: fees get cheaper, the network handles more traffic, and Ethereum becomes a more credible rails layer for stablecoins and tokenized assets.
ETH staking yields currently sit around 3–4% annually, which adds a carry component most blue chips can’t offer.
BNB’s investment case rests on two things: Binance’s continued market share dominance (still the largest CEX by volume), and BNB Chain’s growing ecosystem beyond the exchange.
Ines is the Evergreen Editor at Cryptonews, where she edits, fact-checks, and creates content briefs on blockchain and cryptocurrency.
Active in the industry since 2023, she first became fascinated...
Ethereum is a consistent market leader and the leading layer 1, forming the foundation of DeFi, DePin, and much of the crypto infrastructure.
Ethereum is expected to continue to perform well as profits rotate out of Bitcoin and find its way into the Ethereum ecosystem.
BNB Chain’s 2026 upgrades focus on speed, smoother trading during traffic spikes, and better reliability.
The chain is also moving to a dual-client setup, so one client prioritizes stability while the other pushes performance.
If you use DeFi often, that combination can make BNB more practical to hold and use.

For 2026, many analysts point to Bitcoin for its liquidity and macro hedge appeal, but Ethereum gets cited more often as having the most overall potential due to network activity, developer ecosystem, smart contract dominance, and upcoming upgrades.
Meme coins like Dogecoin and Pepe also rank among the most actively traded tokens.
The best long-term crypto assets represent large markets with millions of users and high trading volumes.
Historically, crypto assets, particularly Bitcoin and Ethereum, have benefited when liquidity conditions improve.
Bitcoin, Ethereum, and XRP are established ecosystems with entire markets built around them.
They are suitable for conservative investors still open to crypto exposure.
Not exactly, Bitcoin is the first and most well-known cryptocurrency, but the term “crypto” refers to the entire category of digital assets, including Ethereum, Solana, and other altcoins.
The most popular cryptocurrencies have a large market cap and many users, for example, Bitcoin (BTC), Ethereum (ETH), BNB (BNB), XRP (XRP), and Solana (SOL).

extraction.body: XRP Leads Crypto Losses as Ethereum, Dogecoin Prices Crater Alongside Bitcoin XRP was the worst-performing altcoin among the leading cryptocurrencies Thursday morning, showing a 15% drop over the last 24 hours as markets swing bearish and Bitcoin extends its losses . At the time of writing, XRP was trading for $1.30 after having dropped roughly 28% in the past week, according to crypto price aggregator CoinGecko. An earlier dip to $1.28 marked the lowest price for the Ripple-linked asset since November 2024, when XRP surged in the wake of President Trump's election win. It's also the biggest daily drop of any coin in the top 100 cryptocurrencies by market cap over the last day. Ethereum was recently trading at $1,985 after plunging 6% on the day and losing about 30% of its value in the last week, while original meme coin Dogecoin is down about 8% on the day to $0.09, shedding nearly 19% of its value over the past seven days. BNB was recently changing hands for $666 after having dropped 9% in the past day, losing 23% in the past seven days. Solana had dipped to $85, after falling about 8% in the past day, and was 27% lower than it was this time last week. Bitcoin dove below the $67,000 mark Thursday morning, but was recently trading just above $68,000. extraction.body: The AI amulet has become a bit of a cliché in the tech industry — devices like Friend have turned the idea of physical AI into little more than an exercise in eye-rolling for many consumers. But that hasn’t stopped Meta from jumping into the arena with its own AI wearable, called Muse Charm, which is designed to give consumers another way to stay connected to its recently launched, and already popular, personal AI agent, Muse. The device, which CEO Mark Zuckerberg revealed in a “one more thing” moment during the company’s annual Connect event, isn’t ready to ship just yet. Zuckerberg said his team had to “finalize laying out the components” and promised the devices would be “ready to ship in time for the holidays in December.” The Muse agent, which is now embodied by a cute digital avatar known within the company as Jolly, lives inside the palm-sized totem that users can carry in their pockets or attach to a keychain. The device comes with a tiny screen that displays the avatar representing the agent. Users can talk to the device, which can then presumably carry out tasks on their behalf. “We packed the whole Muse experience, including the whole real-time voice and avatar stack, into something that fits on a keychain and is always available to talk to,” Zuckerberg said during Wednesday’s keynote. “You just go ahead and tap here in the fingerprint sensor in the corner, and you can start talking without having to unlock a phone or open an app.” Zuckerberg added: “So if you’re not wearing glasses, this is going to be by far the fastest way to talk to your Muse and to show what’s going on around you.” Appropriate for what it offers, the gadget has a quasi-Tamagotchi feel to it — a lightweight, personality-filled device designed to keep users always connected to Meta’s software. It also feels like a relatviely low-stakes way for the social media giant to experiment with AI wearables while also offering yet another way to distribute its AI agent to the masses. sources.title: Meta to release Muse Charm, a Tamagotchi-like device for the Muse AI agent
passages: Meta has a new way to talk to its AI without putting on a pair of glasses.At the end of Wednesday's Meta Connect keynote, CEO Mark Zuckerberg unveiled Muse Charm, a small, always-on handheld device built around Muse, Meta's AI assistant.
Meta describes it as a personal agent that can set goals, share ideas, and run tasks in the background, and users can customize its personality and voice.
Meta did not announce a price and said more details will come later.The device enters a category with a rocky track record.

sources.title: Meta’s Muse Charm Is a Tamagotchi-Style Puck for Its AI Agent, Shipping This December - Shane the Gamer
passages: Our take: Muse’s download numbers are real and worth paying attention to, but a keychain puck is a much harder sell than an app update.
Meta has form here, plenty of hardware side-bets from this company have quietly died within a year.
December will tell us whether Muse Charm ships as a real product or just as a Connect-stage tease that never gets a price tag.
On the official Connect blog, Meta kept the description brief, calling it “a delightful and fun device built for you to talk and interact with your Muse.”
Zuckerberg said it’s not finalized yet but that Meta is planning to have it ship “in time for the holidays” in December.
That timeline was echoed by outside coverage of the keynote, which likewise pegged the device to a holiday-season shipping window rather than a firm date or price.
Meta’s Muse app itself only launched on September 8 and has already had a genuinely strong run.
By the following week, Muse was the most popular free app in the iPhone’s App Store and had been downloaded more than 2.5 million times since launch.
Muse Charm was one piece of a wider push to get the agent off the phone screen entirely.
Meta says it is working to bring Muse to its AI glasses, extending the assistant from phones and computers to a device that can hear a request while its wearer is driving, cooking or exercising.

On glasses, Meta says Muse will be able to guide a personalized workout, log meals, offer nutrition information, help buy products a wearer sees, book appointments, check flight prices and search for replacement parts.
No price has been confirmed for Muse Charm, and Meta hasn’t detailed battery life, connectivity or whether it needs to pair with a phone to work.
The app is built to go further than a normal chatbot.
Muse already lets you shape that character before it ever reaches your keychain.
Zuckerberg demoed exactly that onstage, having reportedly named his own Muse Agrippa, a Roman figure mostly known for military successes.
That’s an ambitious list for a product line Meta itself frames as still in progress.
Meta has not disclosed a user count, revenue figure or product-specific budget for Muse, so the app store charts remain the only hard numbers available right now.

extraction.body: Mark Zuckerberg closed out Meta Connect 2026 with a surprise “one more thing.” Onstage on September 23, he pulled out a small puck-shaped gadget and told the crowd it exists purely so you can carry your Muse AI agent around and talk to it on the move. Meta calls it Muse Charm, a “one more thing” reveal described as a little puck about the size of an Apple Watch, built for talking to your Muse agent. On the official Connect blog, Meta kept the description brief, calling it “a delightful and fun device built for you to talk and interact with your Muse.” The gaming crowd reacted fast, and not always kindly, to the idea of a pocket AI pet on a keychain: The comparison to a Tamagotchi isn’t a stretch. Zuckerberg revealed a little keychain device that holds your Muse AI character, with a screen showing the Muse mascot that you can carry around with you. It’s built to sit apart from your phone, so the agent you’ve spent weeks customising has a physical body you can glance at. Muse already lets you shape that character before it ever reaches your keychain. Users can name their agent, create an avatar and customize how it communicates, right down to accent and speaking pace, according to Meta’s own product framing. Zuckerberg demoed exactly that onstage, having reportedly named his own Muse Agrippa, a Roman figure mostly known for military successes. We’ll say it straight: strapping a screen-and-mic puck to your keys so you can chat to a chatbot mascot is a strange pitch for a company that spent three years trying to sell everyone on legless VR avatars instead. It’s a fun idea. Whether anyone actually wants to talk out loud to a keychain in public is a different question entirely. Meta isn’t treating Muse Charm as a finished product. Zuckerberg said it’s not finalized yet but that Meta is planning to have it ship “in time for the holidays” in December. That timeline was echoed by outside coverage of the keynote, which likewise pegged the device to a holiday-season shipping window rather than a firm date or price. No price has been confirmed for Muse Charm, and Meta hasn’t detailed battery life, connectivity or whether it needs to pair with a phone to work. Given how late in development Zuckerberg admitted the device is, expect more specifics to land closer to a holiday launch rather than at retail preorder. Muse Charm doesn’t exist in a vacuum. Meta’s Muse app itself only launched on September 8 and has already had a genuinely strong run. Meta’s Muse AI personal agent tool overtook ChatGPT as the leading free iOS app in the US, with 730,000 downloads over roughly five days following its September 8 release, according to analytics firm Sensor Tower. By the following week, Muse was the most popular free app in the iPhone’s App Store and had been downloaded more than 2.5 million times since launch. The app is built to go further than a normal chatbot. Muse exists in a chat interface similar to a text thread but is designed to be more proactive and long-running than typical chatbots, and the agent runs on a dedicated virtual machine in Meta’s cloud, using a built-in browser that’s visible to the user. Meta’s own pricing splits users across a free tier and two paid options: a free tier as well as two subscription options, at $20 per month and $100 per month. Meta Superintelligence Labs chief Alexandr Wang argued most people won’t need to pay at all. “For the vast majority of users, they should be able to do what they need to within the free tier,” Wang told Axios. Muse Charm was one piece of a wider push to get the agent off the phone screen entirely. Meta says it is working to bring Muse to its AI glasses, extending the assistant from phones and computers to a device that can hear a request while its wearer is driving, cooking or exercising. On glasses, Meta says Muse will be able to guide a personalized workout, log meals, offer nutrition information, help buy products a wearer sees, book appointments, check flight prices and search for replacement parts. That’s an ambitious list for a product line Meta itself frames as still in progress. The September 23 announcement at Meta Connect describes an integration still in development, and Meta hasn’t published usage figures tied specifically to the glasses rollout. Meta has not disclosed a user count, revenue figure or product-specific budget for Muse, so the app store charts remain the only hard numbers available right now. Our take: Muse’s download numbers are real and worth paying attention to, but a keychain puck is a much harder sell than an app update. passages: Mark Zuckerberg closed out Meta Connect 2026 with a surprise “one more thing.” Onstage on September 23, he pulled out a small puck-shaped gadget and told the crowd it exists purely so you can carry your Muse AI agent around and talk to it on the move.

Meta calls it Muse Charm, a “one more thing” reveal described as a little puck about the size of an Apple Watch, built for talking to your Muse agent. On the official Connect blog, Meta kept the description brief, calling it “a delightful and fun device built for you to talk and interact with your Muse.”
The gaming crowd reacted fast, and not always kindly, to the idea of a pocket AI pet on a keychain:

The comparison to a Tamagotchi isn’t a stretch. Zuckerberg revealed a little keychain device that holds your Muse AI character, with a screen showing the Muse mascot that you can carry around with you. It’s built to sit apart from your phone, so the agent you’ve spent weeks customising has a physical body you can glance at.

Muse already lets you shape that character before it ever reaches your keychain. Users can name their agent, create an avatar and customize how it communicates, right down to accent and speaking pace, according to Meta’s own product framing. Zuckerberg demoed exactly that onstage, having reportedly named his own Muse Agrippa, a Roman figure mostly known for military successes.

We’ll say it straight: strapping a screen-and-mic puck to your keys so you can chat to a chatbot mascot is a strange pitch for a company that spent three years trying to sell everyone on legless VR avatars instead. It’s a fun idea. Whether anyone actually wants to talk out loud to a keychain in public is a different question entirely.

Meta isn’t treating Muse Charm as a finished product. Zuckerberg said it’s not finalized yet but that Meta is planning to have it ship “in time for the holidays” in December. That timeline was echoed by outside coverage of the keynote, which likewise pegged the device to a holiday-season shipping window rather than a firm date or price.

No price has been confirmed for Muse Charm, and Meta hasn’t detailed battery life, connectivity or whether it needs to pair with a phone to work. Given how late in development Zuckerberg admitted the device is, expect more specifics to land closer to a holiday launch rather than at retail preorder.

Muse Charm doesn’t exist in a vacuum. Meta’s Muse app itself only launched on September 8 and has already had a genuinely strong run. Meta’s Muse AI personal agent tool overtook ChatGPT as the leading free iOS app in the US, with 730,000 downloads over roughly five days following its September 8 release, according to analytics firm Sensor Tower. By the following week, Muse was the most popular free app in the iPhone’s App Store and had been downloaded more than 2.5 million times since launch.

The app is built to go further than a normal chatbot. Muse exists in a chat interface similar to a text thread but is designed to be more proactive and long-running than typical chatbots, and the agent runs on a dedicated virtual machine in Meta’s cloud, using a built-in browser that’s visible to the user. Meta’s own pricing splits users across a free tier and two paid options: a free tier as well as two subscription options, at $20 per month and $100 per month.

Meta Superintelligence Labs chief Alexandr Wang argued most people won’t need to pay at all. “For the vast majority of users, they should be able to do what they need to within the free tier,” Wang told Axios.

Muse Charm was one piece of a wider push to get the agent off the phone screen entirely. Meta says it is working to bring Muse to its AI glasses, extending the assistant from phones and computers to a device that can hear a request while its wearer is driving, cooking or exercising. On glasses, Meta says Muse will be able to guide a personalized workout, log meals, offer nutrition information, help buy products a wearer sees, book appointments, check flight prices and search for replacement parts.

That’s an ambitious list for a product line Meta itself frames as still in progress. The September 23 announcement at Meta Connect describes an integration still in development, and Meta hasn’t published usage figures tied specifically to the glasses rollout. Meta has not disclosed a user count, revenue figure or product-specific budget for Muse, so the app store charts remain the only hard numbers available right now.

Our take: Muse’s download numbers are real and worth paying attention to, but a keychain puck is a much harder sell than an app update. Meta has form here, plenty of hardware side-bets from this company have quietly died within a year. December will tell us whether Muse Charm ships as a real product or just as a Connect-stage tease that never gets a price tag.

extraction.body: The AI amulet has become a bit of a cliché in the tech industry — devices like Friend have turned the idea of physical AI into little more than an exercise in eye-rolling for many consumers. But that hasn’t stopped Meta from jumping into the arena with its own AI wearable, called Muse Charm, which is designed to give consumers another way to stay connected to its recently launched, and already popular, personal AI agent, Muse. The device, which CEO Mark Zuckerberg revealed in a “one more thing” moment during the company’s annual Connect event, isn’t ready to ship just yet. Zuckerberg said his team had to “finalize laying out the components” and promised the devices would be “ready to ship in time for the holidays in December.” The Muse agent, which is now embodied by a cute digital avatar known within the company as Jolly, lives inside the palm-sized totem that users can carry in their pockets or attach to a keychain. The device comes with a tiny screen that displays the avatar representing the agent. Users can talk to the device, which can then presumably carry out tasks on their behalf. “We packed the whole Muse experience, including the whole real-time voice and avatar stack, into something that fits on a keychain and is always available to talk to,” Zuckerberg said during Wednesday’s keynote. “You just go ahead and tap here in the fingerprint sensor in the corner, and you can start talking without having to unlock a phone or open an app.” Zuckerberg added: “So if you’re not wearing glasses, this is going to be by far the fastest way to talk to your Muse and to show what’s going on around you.” Appropriate for what it offers, the gadget has a quasi-Tamagotchi feel to it — a lightweight, personality-filled device designed to keep users always connected to Meta’s software. It also feels like a relatviely low-stakes way for the social media giant to experiment with AI wearables while also offering yet another way to distribute its AI agent to the masses. extraction.body: Mark Zuckerberg closed out Meta Connect 2026 with a surprise “one more thing.” Onstage on September 23, he pulled out a small puck-shaped gadget and told the crowd it exists purely so you can carry your Muse AI agent around and talk to it on the move. Zuckerberg revealed a little keychain device that holds your Muse AI character, with a screen showing the Muse mascot that you can carry around with you. It’s built to sit apart from your phone, so the agent you’ve spent weeks customising has a physical body you can glance at. Muse already lets you shape that character before it ever reaches your keychain. Users can name their agent, create an avatar and customize how it communicates, right down to accent and speaking pace, according to Meta’s own product framing. Zuckerberg demoed exactly that onstage, having reportedly named his own Muse Agrippa, a Roman figure mostly known for military successes. We’ll say it straight: strapping a screen-and-mic puck to your keys so you can chat to a chatbot mascot is a strange pitch for a company that spent three years trying to sell everyone on legless VR avatars instead. It’s a fun idea. Whether anyone actually wants to talk out loud to a keychain in public is a different question entirely. Meta isn’t treating Muse Charm as a finished product. Zuckerberg said it’s not finalized yet but that Meta is planning to have it ship “in time for the holidays” in December. That timeline was echoed by outside coverage of the keynote, which likewise pegged the device to a holiday-season shipping window rather than a firm date or price. No price has been confirmed for Muse Charm, and Meta hasn’t detailed battery life, connectivity or whether it needs to pair with a phone to work. Given how late in development Zuckerberg admitted the device is, expect more specifics to land closer to a holiday launch rather than at retail preorder. Muse Charm doesn’t exist in a vacuum. Meta’s Muse app itself only launched on September 8 and has already had a genuinely strong run. Meta’s Muse AI personal agent tool overtook ChatGPT as the leading free iOS app in the US, with 730,000 downloads over roughly five days following its September 8 release, according to analytics firm Sensor Tower. By the following week, Muse was the most popular free app in the iPhone’s App Store and had been downloaded more than 2.5 million times since launch. The app is built to go further than a normal chatbot. Muse exists in a chat interface similar to a text thread but is designed to be more proactive and long-running than typical chatbots, and the agent runs on a dedicated virtual machine in Meta’s cloud, using a built-in browser that’s visible to the user. Meta’s own pricing splits users across a free tier and two paid options: a free tier as well as two subscription options, at $20 per month and $100 per month. Meta Superintelligence Labs chief Alexandr Wang argued most people won’t need to pay at all. “For the vast majority of users, they should be able to do what they need to within the free tier,” Wang told Axios. Muse Charm was one piece of a wider push to get the agent off the phone screen entirely. Meta says it is working to bring Muse to its AI glasses, extending the assistant from phones and computers to a device that can hear a request while its wearer is driving, cooking or exercising. On glasses, Meta says Muse will be able to guide a personalized workout, log meals, offer nutrition information, help buy products a wearer sees, book appointments, check flight prices and search for replacement parts. That’s an ambitious list for a product line Meta itself frames as still in progress. The September 23 announcement at Meta Connect describes an integration still in development, and Meta hasn’t published usage figures tied specifically to the glasses rollout. Meta has not disclosed a user count, revenue figure or product-specific budget for Muse, so the app store charts remain the only hard numbers available right now. Our take: Muse’s download numbers are real and worth paying attention to, but a keychain puck is a much harder sell than an app update. Meta has form here, plenty of hardware side-bets from this company have quietly died within a year. sources.title: Gov. JB Pritzker assembling Illinois Artificial Intelligence Cabinet to assess AI threats - Chicago Sun-Times
passages: The Democratic governor signed an executive order Tuesday establishing the Illinois Artificial Intelligence Cabinet to assess “the various risks posed by Al to the safety of Illinois residents and the critical infrastructure residents rely on.”

JB Pritzker is convening a panel of experts to advise state officials on the potential threats of artificial intelligence as a growing number of industry leaders warn the burgeoning, self-improving technology could spell doomsday for humanity if left unchecked.

Pritzker will name his AI Cabinet members “in the coming weeks” to work alongside numerous state agency leaders, including from the Department of Innovation and Technology, the Department of Public Health and the Illinois Emergency Management Agency.
“Illinois has already enacted nation-leading laws that hold Big Tech accountable and today I’m taking executive action to keep this a priority,” Pritzker said.

They’re expected to come from backgrounds in academia, law, ethics and governance, and provide recommendations on potential public safety threats, protecting public assets and evaluating possible regulations, according to Pritzker’s office.
From WBUR and NPR, co-hosted by Robin Young and Scott Tong, with news from Chicago from WBEZ’s Lisa Labuz.

The unpaid group, which will formulate policy proposals through 2027, will analyze and assess “the various risks posed by AI to the safety of Illinois residents and the critical infrastructure residents rely on.”

extraction.body: SPRINGFIELD — Gov. JB Pritzker is setting up a new group within state government to explore more regulations for artificial intelligence as calls grow across the country for new restrictions. Pritzker signed an executive order on Tuesday to establish an AI Cabinet made up of experts and representatives from several state agencies. The unpaid group, which will formulate policy proposals through 2027, will analyze and assess “the various risks posed by AI to the safety of Illinois residents and the critical infrastructure residents rely on.” It’s the latest move by Illinois to tackle state-focused AI regulation as the federal government continues to take a hands-off approach , even as industry insiders sound the alarm on the technology’s capabilities. A former Anthropic and OpenAI researcher alleged in an explosive social media post earlier this month that AI companies are building a tool that could become “out of control” and pose a threat to human existence by 2030. “Artificial Intelligence has enormous potential to transform our everyday lives, but when experts and industry leaders sound the alarm bell, urge us to slow down, and ask for guardrails, we should listen,” Pritzker said in a statement. The cabinet will formulate policies and procedures to protect Illinois residents and public assets like water systems, education and information systems from threats posed by AI. It will also analyze “emerging AI incidents and share lessons learned” from them. The advisory group will also make policy recommendations on risk management and assess the feasibility, timeframe and any other challenges for implementing them. The cabinet will consider regulations tying data center incentives or operational approval to a company’s ability to meet safety, accountability and transparency standards. It will also look into addressing strain on the energy grid from data centers, evaluating how state procurement and contracting practices can incorporate AI safety and accountability measures, and assessing if existing legal options are good enough to hold AI companies that cause harm accountable. Illinois lawmakers have already taken steps to regulate AI. Pritzker signed Senate Bill 315 in July, also known as the Artificial Intelligence Safety Measures Act , which increases transparency and accountability requirements for the largest artificial intelligence models — those that generate more than $500 million in annual revenue and are trained using massive computing power. It establishes new reporting standards for the possibility that the AI model could be used for large-scale harm, such as by helping create a chemical, biological or nuclear weapon or committing cyber-attacks. It also made Illinois the first state to require annual audits of AI. The law takes effect in 2028. Since the whistleblower came forward earlier this month, Pritzker has been aggressively calling on Congress to step in. “It should be among the top priorities, but don't misunderstand, it is dangerous and it's dangerous on the level of nuclear weapons,” Pritzker said on ABC’s Sunday morning news show . “So that's why it needs to be an international endeavor. Pritzker has urged Congress to immediately begin holding hearings on AI safety and impose national standards. “Artificial Intelligence has enormous potential to transform our everyday lives, but when experts and industry leaders sound the alarm bell, urge us to slow down, and ask for guardrails, we should listen,” Pritzker said in a statement.

The cabinet will formulate policies and procedures to protect Illinois residents and public assets like water systems, education and information systems from threats posed by AI. It will also analyze “emerging AI incidents and share lessons learned” from them.
The advisory group will also make policy recommendations on risk management and assess the feasibility, timeframe and any other challenges for implementing them.

The cabinet will consider regulations tying data center incentives or operational approval to a company’s ability to meet safety, accountability and transparency standards. It will also look into addressing strain on the energy grid from data centers, evaluating how state procurement and contracting practices can incorporate AI safety and accountability measures, and assessing if existing legal options are good enough to hold AI companies that cause harm accountable.
Illinois lawmakers have already taken steps to regulate AI.

Pritzker signed Senate Bill 315 in July, also known as the Artificial Intelligence Safety Measures Act , which increases transparency and accountability requirements for the largest artificial intelligence models — those that generate more than $500 million in annual revenue and are trained using massive computing power. It establishes new reporting standards for the possibility that the AI model could be used for large-scale harm, such as by helping create a chemical, biological or nuclear weapon or committing cyber-attacks.
It also made Illinois the first state to require annual audits of AI. The law takes effect in 2028.
Since the whistleblower came forward earlier this month, Pritzker has been aggressively calling on Congress to step in.

“It should be among the top priorities, but don't misunderstand, it is dangerous and it's dangerous on the level of nuclear weapons,” Pritzker said on ABC’s Sunday morning news show . “So that's why it needs to be an international endeavor.
Pritzker has urged Congress to immediately begin holding hearings on AI safety and impose national standards.

Gov. JB Pritzker speaks at the signing of the Artificial Intelligence (AI) Safety Measures Act in the Loop July 6.

Gov. JB Pritzker is convening a panel of experts to advise state officials on the potential threats of artificial intelligence as a growing number of industry leaders warn the burgeoning, self-improving technology could spell doomsday for humanity if left unchecked.

The Democratic governor signed an executive order Tuesday establishing the Illinois Artificial Intelligence Cabinet to assess “the various risks posed by Al to the safety of Illinois residents and the critical infrastructure residents rely on.”

Pritzker will name his AI Cabinet members “in the coming weeks” to work alongside numerous state agency leaders, including from the Department of Innovation and Technology, the Department of Public Health and the Illinois Emergency Management Agency.

They’re expected to come from backgrounds in academia, law, ethics and governance, and provide recommendations on potential public safety threats, protecting public assets and evaluating possible regulations, according to Pritzker’s office.

His order comes in the wake of former Anthropic AI researcher Jacob Coxon’s media blitz this month warning that aggressive industry development in the absence of federal regulation “could kill us all by the end of the decade.”
OpenAI CEO Sam Altman, Meta chairman Mark Zuckerberg and other AI executives have emphasized the need for broader safety measures.

“Artificial Intelligence has enormous potential to transform our everyday lives, but when experts and industry leaders sound the alarm bell, urge us to slow down, and ask for guardrails, we should listen,” Pritzker said in a statement.
In July, Pritzker signed a package of state-level AI regulations into law that mark some of the most stringent in the nation, requiring frontier developers to submit to annual independent audits.
Pritzker, who has done little to quell speculation about his own presidential ambitions, has blasted President Donald Trump for his administration’s lax approach to AI regulation.

“Illinois has already enacted nation-leading laws that hold Big Tech accountable and today I’m taking executive action to keep this a priority,” Pritzker said. “Congress and the White House need to treat AI risks with urgency, but in the meantime, Illinois won’t wait because it is our foremost responsibility to prepare and protect Illinoisans.”

University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign Chancellor Charles Isbell said in a statement that his institution is “eager to help the state navigate the current challenges and opportunities that AI brings.”

“As a land-grant institution, we are committed to innovation for the public good and to developing human-centered AI that protects privacy, reduces bias, strengthens democratic institutions, uses energy wisely, and creates value for workers, companies and communities,” Isbell said.

extraction.body: SPRINGFIELD — Gov. JB Pritzker is setting up a new group within state government to explore more regulations for artificial intelligence as calls grow across the country for new restrictions. Pritzker signed an executive order on Tuesday to establish an AI Cabinet made up of experts and representatives from several state agencies. The unpaid group, which will formulate policy proposals through 2027, will analyze and assess “the various risks posed by AI to the safety of Illinois residents and the critical infrastructure residents rely on.” It’s the latest move by Illinois to tackle state-focused AI regulation as the federal government continues to take a hands-off approach , even as industry insiders sound the alarm on the technology’s capabilities. A former Anthropic and OpenAI researcher alleged in an explosive social media post earlier this month that AI companies are building a tool that could become “out of control” and pose a threat to human existence by 2030. “Artificial Intelligence has enormous potential to transform our everyday lives, but when experts and industry leaders sound the alarm bell, urge us to slow down, and ask for guardrails, we should listen,” Pritzker said in a statement. The cabinet will formulate policies and procedures to protect Illinois residents and public assets like water systems, education and information systems from threats posed by AI. It will also analyze “emerging AI incidents and share lessons learned” from them. The advisory group will also make policy recommendations on risk management and assess the feasibility, timeframe and any other challenges for implementing them. The cabinet will consider regulations tying data center incentives or operational approval to a company’s ability to meet safety, accountability and transparency standards. It will also look into addressing strain on the energy grid from data centers, evaluating how state procurement and contracting practices can incorporate AI safety and accountability measures, and assessing if existing legal options are good enough to hold AI companies that cause harm accountable. Illinois lawmakers have already taken steps to regulate AI. Pritzker signed Senate Bill 315 in July, also known as the Artificial Intelligence Safety Measures Act , which increases transparency and accountability requirements for the largest artificial intelligence models — those that generate more than $500 million in annual revenue and are trained using massive computing power. It establishes new reporting standards for the possibility that the AI model could be used for large-scale harm, such as by helping create a chemical, biological or nuclear weapon or committing cyber-attacks. It also made Illinois the first state to require annual audits of AI. The law takes effect in 2028. Since the whistleblower came forward earlier this month, Pritzker has been aggressively calling on Congress to step in. “It should be among the top priorities, but don't misunderstand, it is dangerous and it's dangerous on the level of nuclear weapons,” Pritzker said on ABC’s Sunday morning news show . “So that's why it needs to be an international endeavor. Pritzker has urged Congress to immediately begin holding hearings on AI safety and impose national standards.
